question.text: Under the Code of Conduct in the Fourth Schedule of SEBI (AIF) Regulations, which of the following is NOT a prescribed obligation of an AIF Manager?

answer.text: Have written policies and procedures to identify, monitor and mitigate conflicts of interest
Operate the fund in the interest of all investors, not just the sponsor or a select class
Guarantee a minimum rate of return to investors via capital-protection mechanisms
Have written policies and procedures to comply with anti-money-laundering laws

explanation.text: The Logic: The Fourth Schedule Code of Conduct requires managing in interest of ALL investors, conflict-of-interest policies, AML compliance, effective risk management, accurate disclosures, abstention from unethical sales. GUARANTEE of returns is explicitly PROHIBITED — Sponsor/Manager 'should abstain from assuring returns'. The Trap: Options A, B, D are direct Code obligations. Option C contradicts both the Code and PFUTP. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B (Distributors), III-A (Compliance) test Code. XIX-E from Manager-side. Manager's Pro-Tip: For marketing decks, strip out any phrase that could be read as 'assured return'. Even 'target IRR' needs cautious framing; 'benchmark' or 'objective' is safer.
